what: L3Harris Technologies is a US defence contractor. It makes tactical radios, electronic warfare systems, night vision, space sensors and, since buying Aerojet Rocketdyne, rocket motors for missiles.
customers: The US Department of Defense and intelligence agencies, allied governments in more than 100 countries, and prime contractors.
money: space sensors, intelligence systems and avionics
moat: Programmes written into defence budgets for years ahead, with classified work and qualified production lines that competitors cannot enter quickly.
risks: US defence budget decisions drive almost all revenue
Debt of about $11 billion from the Aerojet purchase
Fixed-price development contracts have caused losses across the industry
Operating margin of 10% is lower than its larger peers'
opportunities: Solid rocket motors are in short supply industry-wide as missile stockpiles are rebuilt
Analysts see about 30% upside from current levels
European and Asian allies are raising defence spending
watch: The book-to-bill ratio and margin progress at Aerojet Rocketdyne.
